question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_b: A device used only to inspect fifth wheel clearance
choice_c: A hydraulic brake modulator for triples
choice_d: A type of air storage tank used on the rear trailer
explanation: A converter dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.1/7.2 - Coupling and Uncoupling

question: How do you release the dolly's brakes before wheeling it into position (if it does not have spring brakes)?
choice_a: By pulling the trailer emergency valve
choice_b: By opening the air tank petcock
choice_c: By disconnecting the safety chains
explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock (or, if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When using the tractor and first semitrailer to pick up the converter dolly, what must be done to the dolly support before pulling it into position?
choice_a: It must be removed entirely
choice_b: It must be lowered completely to the ground
choice_c: It must be secured in the raised position
explanation: When picking up the converter dolly, secure the dolly support in the raised position before pulling the dolly into position in front of the second trailer.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
question: When connecting a converter dolly to the rear trailer, the trailer height must be correct. What does "correct" mean?
choice_a: The trailer must be exactly level with the ground
choice_b: The trailer must be higher than the tractor frame
choice_c: The trailer height does not matter for coupling
choice_d: The trailer must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so it is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
explanation: Trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
question: How do you test the coupling after backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer?
choice_a: By pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_b: By visually inspecting only, no physical test needed
choice_c: By driving forward at normal speed
explanation: Test coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
question: What should a driver look for during a visual check of the fifth wheel coupling?
choice_a: The color of the kingpin
choice_b: No space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin
choice_c: The alcohol evaporator fluid level
choice_d: The position of the wig wag device
explanation: Make a visual check of coupling: no space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on kingpin.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
question: After connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords when coupling a converter dolly to the second trailer, what should be closed?
choice_a: The dolly's landing gear
choice_b: The tractor protection valve
choice_c: The converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer
explanation: Close converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at rear of second trailer (service and emergency shut-offs).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
question: After raising the landing gear completely during coupling, how do you check that air pressure is reaching the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: By pulling the pintle hook
choice_b: By checking the wig wag device
choice_c: By reading the application pressure gauge only
choice_d: By pushing the "air supply" knob in and opening the emergency line shut-off at the rear of the second trailer to check for air
explanation: Charge trailer brakes (push "air supply" knob in), and check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.1 - Coupling Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles, what should be done if the second trailer doesn't have spring brakes?
choice_a: Chock the wheels of the second trailer
choice_b: Remove the landing gear entirely
choice_c: Disconnect the pintle hook first
explanation: Chock wheels of second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes, after parking the rig in a straight line and applying parking brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.2 - Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why is the landing gear of the second semitrailer lowered slightly before pulling the dolly out?
choice_a: To increase ground clearance
choice_b: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_c: To disconnect the electric lines
choice_d: To test the trailer emergency brakes
explanation: Lower landing gear of second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.2 - Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: After releasing the converter dolly fifth wheel latch, how do you separate the dolly from the rear semitrailer?
choice_a: Lift the rear semitrailer with a jack
choice_b: Reverse the tractor into the dolly
choice_c: Slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer
explanation: Slowly pull tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.2 - Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: What warning does the manual give about unlocking the pintle hook on the first semitrailer?
choice_a: Always unlock it before lowering the landing gear
choice_b: It should only be unlocked by a certified mechanic
choice_c: It must be unlocked before releasing the dolly brakes
choice_d: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer, as the tow bar may fly up and cause injury
explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer; the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.2 - Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: After lowering the dolly landing gear and disconnecting safety chains during uncoupling, what should be done to the dolly wheels?
choice_a: Apply converter gear spring brakes or chock the wheels
choice_b: Remove the wheels for inspection
choice_c: Leave them unsecured since the dolly is disconnected
explanation: Apply converter gear spring brakes or chock wheels before releasing the pintle hook and pulling clear of the dolly.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.2 - Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: How do you couple the tractor to the first trailer when assembling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Use a special triples-only fifth wheel
choice_b: Use the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers
choice_c: Attach the dolly first, then the tractor
choice_d: Couple the rear trailer before the first trailer
explanation: Couple tractor to first trailer using the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.3 - Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is uncoupled first?
choice_a: The first trailer behind the tractor
choice_b: All three trailers simultaneously
choice_c: The third (last) trailer, by pulling the dolly out
explanation: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.2.3 - Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: During a coupling system inspection, where should the locking jaws be positioned around the kingpin?
choice_a: Around the head only
choice_b: Anywhere that provides a tight grip
choice_c: They should not touch the kingpin at all
choice_d: Around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin
explanation: Locking jaws should be around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: What should be checked regarding the fifth wheel release arm during inspection?
choice_a: It should be properly seated with the safety latch/lock engaged
choice_b: It should be disconnected for towing
choice_c: It should be painted yellow
choice_d: It should be removed entirely on doubles
explanation: Check that the release arm is properly seated and the safety latch/lock is engaged.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: What should be checked about the landing gear during a walk-around inspection of doubles/triples?
choice_a: That it is painted a specific color
choice_b: That it is fully raised, with no missing parts and not bent or damaged, and the crank handle is in place and secured
choice_c: That it matches the trailer's VIN number
choice_d: That it has an ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: Landing gear should be fully raised, with no missing parts, not bent or otherwise damaged, and the crank handle in place and secured.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Landing Gear

question: During inspection of double and triple trailers, what position should the shut-off valves be at the rear of the front trailer(s)?
choice_a: Closed
choice_b: Half-open
choice_c: Open
explanation: For double and triple trailer shut-off valves in service and emergency lines: rear of front trailers should be OPEN.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: What position should the shut-off valves be at the rear of the last trailer in a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Open
choice_b: Half-open
choice_c: Disconnected
explanation: Rear of last trailer: CLOSED.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: During inspection, what position should the converter dolly's air tank drain valve be in?
choice_a: Closed
choice_b: Open
choice_c: Half-open
explanation: Converter dolly air tank drain valve: CLOSED.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: When checking that air flows to all trailers on a double or triple, what should you do after pushing in the red "trailer air supply" knob and going to the rear of the rig?
choice_a: Immediately disconnect the light cords
choice_b: Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer and listen for escaping air
choice_c: Release the pintle hook
explanation: Go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer; you should hear air escaping, showing the entire system is charged.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks

question: If you do NOT hear air escaping from both lines during the air flow check on doubles/triples, what should you check?
choice_a: The alcohol evaporator level
choice_b: The ABS malfunction lamp bulb
choice_c: That the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position
explanation: If you do not hear air escaping from both lines, check that the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position; air must reach all the way to the back for all brakes to work.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Tractor Protection Valve
question: When testing the tractor protection valve, what should happen to the trailer air supply control when air pressure is reduced by stepping on and off the brake pedal with the engine off?
choice_a: It should remain in the "normal" position indefinitely
choice_b: It should lock in the "emergency" position permanently
choice_c: It should trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_d: It should pop out (or move from "normal" to "emergency" position) at the manufacturer-specified pressure range, usually 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The trailer air supply control should pop out (or go from "normal" to "emergency" position) when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer, usually within 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Tractor Protection Valve
question: What could happen if the tractor protection valve does not work properly?
choice_a: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control
choice_b: The ABS malfunction lamp will fail to illuminate at startup
choice_c: The dolly landing gear will not raise
explanation: If the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Trailer Emergency Brakes
question: How do you test the trailer emergency brakes on a double or triple?
choice_a: Disconnect the electrical cord and observe the trailer
choice_b: Charge the trailer air system, check the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to confirm the emergency brakes engage
choice_c: Only check the parking brake knob color
choice_d: Test only the service brake pedal
explanation: Charge the trailer air brake system, check the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in the "emergency" position) and pull gently on the trailer to check that the emergency brakes are on.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Trailer Service Brakes
question: How should trailer service brakes be tested according to the manual?
choice_a: Only with the foot pedal at highway speed
choice_b: By disconnecting the dolly from the rig
choice_c: With the hand control (trolley valve), moving the vehicle forward slowly and feeling the brakes come on
choice_d: By checking the alcohol evaporator fluid level
explanation: Test trailer service brakes by checking for normal air pressure, releasing the parking brakes, moving the vehicle forward slowly, and applying trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) to feel them come on.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks
